nodes.text: Softly. The harp holds the last note longer than you would credit.
The Songhouse keeps what happened. Some of it is even true. What do you want kept, or found?

choices.text: Is there a song about deep water?
Sing me the verse nobody sings.

nodes.text: Everything the stones cannot hold. Names, mostly. A ledger forgives, a song forgives twice. When the thinned blood comes up the trail I sing the leaving song for their line, and they cry without knowing why. That is memory working.
There is a listening song. The pearls the storms leave were our ears once, for deep water. There is a fisher on the far coast who is owed that song. If the sea sends her, I will sing it true.

choices.text: The song is whole now. I was there.

nodes.text: You were, and the pearl sits where the harp can see it, and I have not sung it since. Some songs are for having, not for spending. When Denna of the coast comes up the trail at last, it will spend itself, and I intend to be surprised by my own voice when it does.
Yes. The verse is about the grove, and it is not mine to give, and you are the eleventh to ask this season. Elarin keeps a list. He finds it funnier than I do.
